data.name: Babak
data.gender_notes: Babak is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Like a tiger, this name signifies power and bravery. The name Babak carries the meaning “Tiger” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Persian, Arabic. Parents who choose Babak usually hope their child will grow to embody tiger and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Babak represents the fierce and unyielding spirit of a warrior, one who is willing to fight for what they believe in.
data.etymology: Babak belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Tiger.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Babak total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_arabic.name: بابک
in_arabic.meaning: أصل اسم من الألقاب و يُشير إلى الذكاء و البخل و الشجاعة
in_arabic.long_meaning: بابک هو اسم عربي قديم يأتي من الصوت الباب، و يُشير إلى الذكاء و البخل و الشجاعة، و كان يُستخدم في العصور القديمة لوصف أشخاص ذوي شخصيات معقدة، و يَعتبر اسم بابک من أشهر الأسماء في الثقافة الإسلامية، و يُمكن أن يُعد اسم بابک من الأسماء التي تحمل المعاني الأربعة التي ذكرها الإمام الحسن البصري، وهي: الذكاء، البخل، الشجاعة، و التوحيد، و يُعتبر بابک من أشهر الأسماء التي يُستخدمها المسلمون في جميع أنحاء العالم.

in_urdu.name: بابک
in_urdu.meaning: اسم کا اورنگ و شہرت کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے اور ذہانت، بہتے ہوئے اور شجاعت کا تعلق ہوتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: بابک ایک قدیم عربی نام ہے جو صوتی بنیاد پر بنا ہوا ہے اور ذہانت، بہتے ہوئے اور شجاعت کا تعلق ہے۔ اس نام کو قدیم زمانے میں استعمال کیا جاتا تھا اور اس سے متعلق اشخاص کی معقد شخصیت کی نشاندہی کی جاتی تھی۔ ایک قدیم اسلامی نام کے طور پر، بابک کو مسلمانوں کے مختلف خطوں میں ایک بہت زیادہ مقبول نام سمجھا جاتا ہے اور اس کی تیسری معنی کو اکثر مسلمانوں کی ثقافت کا ایک حصہ سمجھا جاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बबक
in_hindi.meaning: इतिहास में एक प्रसिद्ध नाम जो बुद्धिमत्ता, शौर्य और विलासिता का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: बबक एक प्राचीन अरबी नाम है जो शब्दिक अर्थ पर आधारित है और बुद्धिमत्ता, शौर्य और विलासिता का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है। इस नाम का उपयोग प्राचीन काल में किया जाता था और इसके साथ जुड़े व्यक्तियों की जटिल व्यक्तित्व को दर्शाया जाता था। इस्लामिक परंपरा में, बबक एक प्रसिद्ध नाम है जो मुस्लिम समुदाय में बहुत उपयोग किया जाता है और इसकी तीसरी अर्थ अक्सर मुस्लिम संस्कृति का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा मानी जाती है।

in_pashto.name: بابک
in_pashto.meaning: د بابک یوځای او چارې ګټې لري چې د وړمنتیا، غنډی پوهېدو، شجاعت او توحید څخه عبارت دي
in_pashto.long_meaning: د بابک نوم د افغانستان او د پښتنو ثقافت کې ډیر مشهور دی چې د وړمنتیا، غنډی پوهېدو، شجاعت او توحید څخه عبارت دی. دا نوم د افغانستان او د پښتنو تاریخ کې د یو ځانګړي نوم په توګه ډیر مشهور دی. د بابک نوم د پښتنو لپاره یو نوم دی چې د دوی د تاریخ کې یو ځانګړی اهمیت لري.

In these areas, the name is associated with legendary figures of the past, particularly Babak Khorramdin, a 9th-century revolutionary leader who resisted the Abbasid Caliphate’s rule in the area. He led widespread revolts against the foreign oppressors, inspiring a sense of national pride and resistance against foreign domination among the indigenous people.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Babak" can be interpreted as a symbol of courage, resistance, and determination. It is a reminder of the power within each individual to stand up against injustice and oppression, no matter the odds. Additionally, the name may be seen as a connection to the spiritual warrior archetype, embodied in figures such as Babak Khorramdin, who fought not only for political freedom, but also for the spiritual and emotional freedom of their people.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Babak was a Kurdish ruler who led an uprising against the Abbasid Caliphs in the 9th century. The name Babak carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The Abbasid Caliphs ruled the Islamic world from Baghdad during this period. Babak's rebellion, also known as the Babakid revolt, was the largest and most significant challenge to the Abbasid rule in the eastern part of their empire. Babak declared himself the 'King of Kings' and established his capital in the mountainous region of Gurgan and Maragha in present-day Iran.

historical_references.reference: Babak is known for his military and leadership skills, having successfully held out against the Abbasid forces for over a decade.
historical_references.context: Despite initial successes, Babak's rebellion was eventually put down by the Abbasid general Tahir ibn Hubayra. Babak himself was eventually captured and executed, but his rebellion continued to inspire resistance against foreign rule in the region for centuries to come.

modern_usage.modern_context: Babak is a figure from Persian mythology, who is also significant in Iranian history and Middle Eastern folklore. In modern contexts, Babak is a popular character in tabletop role-playing games, where he is often portrayed as a heroic figure leading resistance against invading forces. In fantasy literature, Babak is a common name for characters, often with magical abilities or heroic backgrounds. In anime and manga, Babak is sometimes used as a character name or a place name, reflecting the influence of Middle Eastern mythology and history in Japanese popular culture.
